*This section is non-normative.*

This document defines APIs for requesting access to local multimedia devices, such as microphones or video cameras.

This document also defines the MediaStream API, which provides the means to control where multimedia stream data is consumed, and provides some control over the devices that produce the media. It also exposes information about devices able to capture and render media.

As well as sections marked as non-normative, all authoring guidelines, diagrams, examples, and notes in this specification are non-normative. Everything else in this specification is normative.

The key words *MAY*, *MUST*, *MUST NOT*, *NOT REQUIRED*, and *SHOULD* in this document are to be interpreted as described in [BCP 14](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14) \[[RFC2119](#bib-rfc2119 "Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels")\] \[[RFC8174](#bib-rfc8174 "Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words")\] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

This specification defines conformance criteria that apply to a single product: the User Agent that implements the interfaces that it contains.

Conformance requirements phrased as algorithms or specific steps may be implemented in any manner, so long as the end result is equivalent. (In particular, the algorithms defined in this specification are intended to be easy to follow, and not intended to be performant.)

Implementations that use ECMAScript \[[ECMA-262](#bib-ecma-262 "ECMAScript Language Specification")\] to implement the APIs defined in this specification must implement them in a manner consistent with the ECMAScript Bindings defined in the Web IDL specification \[[WEBIDL](#bib-webidl "Web IDL Standard")\], as this specification uses that specification and terminology.

source

A source is the "thing" providing the source of a media stream track. The source is the broadcaster of the media itself. A source can be a physical webcam, microphone, local video or audio file from the user's hard drive, network resource, or static image. Note that this document describes the use of microphone and camera type sources only, the use of other source types is described in other documents.

An application that has no prior authorization regarding sources is only given the number of available sources, their type and any relationship to other devices. Additional information about sources can become available when applications are authorized to use a source (see [9.2.1 Access control model](#access-control-model)).

Sources **do not** have constraints — tracks have constraints. When a source is connected to a track, it must produce media that conforms to the constraints present on that track, to that track. Multiple tracks can be attached to the same source. [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) processing, such as downsampling, *MAY* be used to ensure that all tracks have appropriate media.

Sources have constrainable properties which have [capabilities](#dfn-capabilities) and [settings](#dfn-settings) exposed on tracks. While the constrainable properties are "owned" by the source, sources *MAY* be able to accommodate different demands at once. For this reason, capabilities are common to any (multiple) tracks that happen to be using the same source, whereas settings *MAY* differ per track (e.g., if two different track objects bound to the same source query capability and settings information, they will get back the same capabilities, but may get different settings that are tailored to satisfy their individual constraints).

Setting (Source Setting)

A setting refers to the immediate, current value of the source's constrainable properties. Settings are always read-only.

A source conditions may dynamically change, such as when a camera switches to a lower frame rate due to low light conditions. In these cases the tracks related to the affected source might not satisfy the set constraints any longer. The platform *SHOULD* try to minimize such excursions as far as possible, but will continue to deliver media even when a temporary or permanent condition exists that prevents satisfying the constraints.

Although settings are a property of the source, they are only exposed to the application through the tracks attached to the source. This is exposed via the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern) interface.

Capability

For each constrainable property, there is a capability that describes whether it is supported by the source and if so, the range of supported values. As with settings, capabilities are exposed to the application via the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern) interface.

The values of the supported capabilities must be normalized to the ranges and enumerated types defined in this specification.

A [`getCapabilities`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-getcapabilities)`()` call on a track returns the same underlying per-source capabilities for all tracks connected to the source.

This API is intentionally simplified. Capabilities are not capable of describing interactions between different values. For instance, it is not possible to accurately describe the capabilities of a camera that can produce a high resolution video stream at a low frame rate and lower resolutions at a higher frame rate. Capabilities describe the complete range of each value. Interactions between constraints are exposed by attempting to apply constraints.

Constraints

Constraints provide a general control surface that allows applications to both select an appropriate source for a track and, once selected, to influence how a source operates.

Constraints limit the range of operating modes that a source can use when providing media for a track. Without provided track constraints, implementations are free to select a source's settings from the full ranges of its supported capabilities. Implementations may also adjust source settings at any time within the bounds imposed by all applied constraints.

[`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia)`()` uses constraints to help select an appropriate source for a track and configure it. Additionally, the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern) interface on tracks includes an API for dynamically changing the track's constraints at any later time.

A track will not be connected to a source using [`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia)`()` if its initial constraints cannot be satisfied. However, the ability to meet the constraints on a track can change over time, and constraints can be changed. If circumstances change such that constraints cannot be met, the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern) interface defines an appropriate error to inform the application. [5\. The model: sources, sinks, constraints, and settings](#the-model-sources-sinks-constraints-and-settings) explains how constraints interact in more detail.

For each constrainable property, a constraint exists whose name corresponds with the relevant source setting name and capability name.

A constraint falls into one of three groups, depending on its place in the constraints structure. The groups are:

-   required constraints are all [non-advanced](#dfn-advanced-constraints) constraints that are [required](#dfn-required).
-   optional basic constraints are the remaining [non-advanced](#dfn-advanced-constraints) constraints.
-   advanced constraints are all constraints specified using the `[advanced](#dom-constraints-advanced)` keyword.

In general, [User Agents](#dfn-user-agent) will have more flexibility to optimize the media streaming experience the fewer constraints are applied, so application authors are strongly encouraged to use [required constraints](#dfn-required-constraints) sparingly.

The two main components in the MediaStream API are the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) and [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) interfaces. The [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object represents media of a single type that originates from one media source in the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent), e.g. video produced by a web camera. A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) is used to group several [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects into one unit that can be recorded or rendered in a media element.

Each [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) can contain zero or more [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects. All tracks in a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) are intended to be synchronized when rendered. This is not a hard requirement, since it might not be possible to synchronize tracks from sources that have different clocks. Different [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) objects do not need to be synchronized.

Note

While the intent is to synchronize tracks, it could be better in some circumstances to permit tracks to lose synchronization. In particular, when tracks are remotely sourced and real-time \[[WEBRTC](#bib-webrtc "WebRTC: Real-Time Communication in Browsers")\], it can be better to allow loss of synchronization than to accumulate delays or risk glitches and other artifacts. Implementations are expected to understand the implications of choices regarding synchronization of playback and the effect that these have on user perception.

A single [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) can represent multi-channel content, such as stereo or 5.1 audio or stereoscopic video, where the channels have a well defined relationship to each other. Information about channels might be exposed through other APIs, such as \[[WEBAUDIO](#bib-webaudio "Web Audio API")\], but this specification provides no direct access to channels.

A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object has an input and an output that represent the combined input and output of all the object's tracks. The output of the [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) controls how the object is rendered, e.g., what is saved if the object is recorded to a file or what is displayed if the object is used in a `[video](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#video)` element. A single [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object can be attached to multiple different outputs at the same time.

A new [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object can be created from existing media streams or tracks using the [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream)`()` constructor. The constructor argument can either be an existing [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object, in which case all the tracks of the given stream are added to the new [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object, or an array of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects. The latter form makes it possible to compose a stream from different source streams.

Both [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) and [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects can be cloned. A cloned [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) contains clones of all member tracks from the original stream. A cloned [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) has a [set of constraints](#constrainable-interface) that is independent of the instance it is cloned from, which allows media from the same source to have different constraints applied for different [consumer](#dfn-consumer)s. The [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object is also used in contexts outside [`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia), such as \[[WEBRTC](#bib-webrtc "WebRTC: Real-Time Communication in Browsers")\].

The MediaStream `constructor` composes a new stream out of existing tracks. It takes an optional argument of type [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) or an array of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects. When the constructor is invoked, the User Agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let stream be a newly constructed [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object.

2.  Initialize stream.[`id`](#dom-mediastream-id) attribute to a newly generated value.

3.  If the constructor's argument is present, run the following steps:

1.  Construct a set of tracks tracks based on the type of argument:

-   A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object:

Let tracks be a set containing all the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects in the [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) [track set](#dfn-track-set).

-   A sequence of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects:

Let tracks be a set containing all the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects in the provided sequence.

2.  For each [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack), track , in tracks, run the following steps:

1.  If track is already in stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set), skip track.

2.  Otherwise, add track to stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set).

4.  Return stream.

The tracks of a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) are stored in a track set. The track set *MUST* contain the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects that correspond to the tracks of the stream. The relative order of the tracks in the set is User Agent defined and the API will never put any requirements on the order. The proper way to find a specific [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object in the set is to look it up by its [`id`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-id).

An object that reads data from the output of a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) is referred to as a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) consumer. The list of [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) consumers currently include media elements (such as `[video](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#video)` and `[audio](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#audio)`) \[[HTML](#bib-html "HTML Standard")\], Web Real-Time Communications (WebRTC; [`RTCPeerConnection`](https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/#dom-rtcpeerconnection)) \[[WEBRTC](#bib-webrtc "WebRTC: Real-Time Communication in Browsers")\], media recording (`MediaRecorder`) \[[mediastream-recording](#bib-mediastream-recording "MediaStream Recording")\], image capture (`ImageCapture`) \[[image-capture](#bib-image-capture "MediaStream Image Capture")\], and web audio ([`MediaStreamAudioSourceNode`](https://www.w3.org/TR/webaudio-1.0/#MediaStreamAudioSourceNode)) \[[WEBAUDIO](#bib-webaudio "Web Audio API")\].

Note

[`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) consumers must be able to handle tracks being added and removed. This behavior is specified per consumer.

A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object is said to be active when it has at least one [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) that has not [ended](#track-ended). A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) that does not have any tracks or only has tracks that are [ended](#track-ended) is inactive.

A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object is said to be audible when it has at least one [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) whose [`[[Kind]]`](#dfn-kind) is [`"audio"`](#dfn-audio) that has not [ended](#track-ended). A [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) that does not have any audio tracks or only has audio tracks that are [ended](#track-ended) is inaudible.

The [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) may update a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream)'s [track set](#dfn-track-set) in response to, for example, an external event. This specification does not specify any such cases, but other specifications using the MediaStream API may. One such example is the WebRTC 1.0 \[[WEBRTC](#bib-webrtc "WebRTC: Real-Time Communication in Browsers")\] specification where the [track set](#dfn-track-set) of a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream), received from another peer, can be updated as a result of changes to the media session.

To add a track track to a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) stream, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  If track is already in stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set), then abort these steps.

2.  Add track to stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set).

3.  [Fire a track event](#dfn-fire-a-track-event) named [`addtrack`](#event-mediastream-addtrack) with track at stream.

To remove a track track from a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) stream, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  If track is not in stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set), then abort these steps.

2.  [Remove](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove) track from stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set).

3.  [Fire a track event](#dfn-fire-a-track-event) named [`removetrack`](#event-mediastream-removetrack) with track at stream.

```
[Exposed=Window]
interface MediaStream : EventTarget {
constructor();
constructor(MediaStream stream);
constructor(sequence<MediaStreamTrack> tracks);
readonly attribute DOMString id;
sequence<MediaStreamTrack> getAudioTracks();
sequence<MediaStreamTrack> getVideoTracks();
sequence<MediaStreamTrack> getTracks();
MediaStreamTrack? getTrackById(DOMString trackId);
undefined addTrack(MediaStreamTrack track);
undefined removeTrack(MediaStreamTrack track);
MediaStream clone();
readonly attribute boolean active;
attribute EventHandler onaddtrack;
attribute EventHandler onremovetrack;
};
```

[`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream)

See the [MediaStream constructor algorithm](#mediastream-constructor)

*No parameters.*

[`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream)

See the [MediaStream constructor algorithm](#mediastream-constructor)

[`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream)

See the [MediaStream constructor algorithm](#mediastream-constructor)

[`id`](#dom-mediastream-id) of type [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString), readonly

The `id` attribute *MUST* return the value to which it was initialized when the object was created.

When a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) is created, the User Agent *MUST* generate an identifier string, and *MUST* initialize the object's [`id`](#dom-mediastream-id) attribute to that string, unless the object is created as part of a special purpose algorithm that specifies how the stream id must be initialized. A good practice is to use a UUID \[[rfc4122](#bib-rfc4122 "A Universally Unique IDentifier (UUID) URN Namespace")\], which is 36 characters long in its canonical form. To avoid fingerprinting, implementations *SHOULD* use the forms in section 4.4 or 4.5 of RFC 4122 when generating UUIDs.

An example of an algorithm that specifies how the stream id must be initialized is the algorithm to associate an incoming network component with a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object. \[[WEBRTC](#bib-webrtc "WebRTC: Real-Time Communication in Browsers")\]

`active` of type [`boolean`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-boolean), readonly

The [`active`](#dom-mediastream-active) attribute *MUST* return `true` if this [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) is [active](#stream-active) and `false` otherwise.

`onaddtrack` of type [`EventHandler`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#eventhandler)

The event type of this event handler is [`addtrack`](#dom-mediastream-addtrack).

`onremovetrack` of type [`EventHandler`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#eventhandler)

The event type of this event handler is [`removetrack`](#dom-mediastream-removetrack).

`getAudioTracks()`

Returns a sequence of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects representing the audio tracks in this stream.

The [`getAudioTracks`](#dom-mediastream-getaudiotracks) method *MUST* return a sequence that represents a snapshot of all the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects in this stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set) whose [`[[Kind]]`](#dfn-kind) is equal to [`"audio"`](#dfn-audio). The conversion from the [track set](#dfn-track-set) to the sequence is [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) defined and the order does not have to be stable between calls.

`getVideoTracks()`

Returns a sequence of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects representing the video tracks in this stream.

The [`getVideoTracks`](#dom-mediastream-getvideotracks) method *MUST* return a sequence that represents a snapshot of all the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects in this stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set) whose [`[[Kind]]`](#dfn-kind) is equal to [`"video"`](#dfn-video). The conversion from the [track set](#dfn-track-set) to the sequence is [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) defined and the order does not have to be stable between calls.

`getTracks()`

Returns a sequence of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects representing all the tracks in this stream.

The [`getTracks`](#dom-mediastream-gettracks) method *MUST* return a sequence that represents a snapshot of all the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects in this stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set), regardless of [`[[Kind]]`](#dfn-kind). The conversion from the [track set](#dfn-track-set) to the sequence is User Agent defined and the order does not have to be stable between calls.

`getTrackById()`

The [`getTrackById`](#dom-mediastream-gettrackbyid) method *MUST* return either a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object from this stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set) whose [`[[Id]]`](#dfn-id) is equal to trackId, or `null`, if no such track exists.

`addTrack()`

Adds the given [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) to this [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream).

When the [`addTrack`](#dom-mediastream-addtrack) method is invoked, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  Let track be the methods argument and stream the [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object on which the method was called.

2.  If track is already in stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set), then abort these steps.

3.  [Add](#dfn-add-a-track) track to stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set).

`removeTrack()`

Removes the given [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object from this [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream).

When the [`removeTrack`](#dom-mediastream-removetrack) method is invoked, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  Let track be the methods argument and stream the [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object on which the method was called.

2.  If track is not in stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set), then abort these steps.

3.  [Remove](#dfn-remove-a-track) track from stream's [track set](#dfn-track-set).

`clone()`

Clones the given [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) and all its tracks.

When the [`clone`](#dom-mediastream-clone)`()` method is invoked, the User Agent *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  Let streamClone be a newly constructed [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object.

2.  Initialize streamClone.[`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream).[`id`](#dom-mediastream-id) to a newly generated value.

3.  [Clone each track](#track-clone) in this [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) object and add the result to streamClone's [track set](#dfn-track-set).

4.  Return streamClone.

User agent code that expects to fire the addtrack or removetrack events is expected to keep the target [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) objects alive by reference from another object. The presence of addtrack or removetrack event listeners does not need to be taken into account when trying to garbage collect [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) objects.

A [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object represents a media source in the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent). An example source is a device connected to the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent). Other specifications may define sources for [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) that override the behavior specified here. Several [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects can represent the same media source, e.g., when the user chooses the same camera in the UI shown by two consecutive calls to [`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia)`()`.

A [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) source defines the following properties:

1.  A source has a MediaStreamTrack source type. It is set to either [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) or a subtype of [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack). By default, it is set to [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack).
2.  A source has MediaStreamTrack source-specific construction steps that are executed when creating a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) from a source. The steps take a newly created [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) as input. By default, the steps are empty.
3.  A source has MediaStreamTrack source-specific clone steps that are executed when cloning a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) of the given source. The steps take the source and destination [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack)s as input. By default, the steps are empty.

The data from a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object does not necessarily have a canonical binary form; for example, it could just be "the video currently coming from the user's video camera". This allows [User Agents](#dfn-user-agent) to manipulate media in whatever fashion is most suitable on the user's platform.

A script can indicate that a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object no longer needs its source with the [`stop`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-stop)`()` method. When all tracks using a source have been stopped or ended by some other means, the source is stopped. If the source is a device exposed by [`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia)`()`, then when the source is stopped, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  Let mediaDevices be the [`MediaDevices`](#dom-mediadevices) object in question.

2.  Let deviceId be the source device's [`deviceId`](#dom-mediadeviceinfo-deviceid).

3.  Set mediaDevices.[`[[devicesLiveMap]]`](#dfn-deviceslivemap)\[deviceId\] to `false`.

4.  If the [permission state](https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/#dfn-permission-state) of the permission associated with the device's kind and deviceId for mediaDevices's [relevant settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#relevant-settings-object), is not "[`granted`](https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/#dom-permissionstate-granted)", then set mediaDevices.[`[[devicesAccessibleMap]]`](#dfn-devicesaccessiblemap)\[deviceId\] to `false`.

To create a MediaStreamTrack with an underlying source, and a mediaDevicesToTieSourceTo, run the following steps:

1.  Let track be a new object of type source's [MediaStreamTrack source type](#dfn-mediastreamtrack-source-type).

Initialize track with the following internal slots:

-   \[\[Source\]\], initialized to source.

-   \[\[Id\]\], initialized to a newly generated unique identifier string. See [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream).[`id`](#dom-mediastream-id) attribute for guidelines on how to generate such an identifier.

-   \[\[Kind\]\], initialized to `"audio"` if source is an audio source, or `"video"` if source is a video source.

-   \[\[Label\]\], initialized to source's label, if provided by the User Agent, or `""` otherwise. [User Agents](#dfn-user-agent) *MAY* label audio and video sources (e.g., "Internal microphone" or "External USB Webcam").

-   \[\[ReadyState\]\], initialized to "[`live`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.live)".

-   \[\[Enabled\]\], initialized to `true`.

-   \[\[Muted\]\], initialized to `true` if source is [muted](#dfn-muted-0), and `false` otherwise.

-   [\[\[Capabilities\]\]](#dfn-capabilities-0), [\[\[Constraints\]\]](#dfn-constraints), and [\[\[Settings\]\]](#dfn-settings-0), all initialized as specified in the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern).
-   \[\[Restrictable\]\], initialized to `false`.

2.  If mediaDevicesToTieSourceTo is not `null`, [tie track source to `MediaDevices`](#dfn-tie-track-source-to-mediadevices) with source and mediaDevicesToTieSourceTo.

3.  Run source's [MediaStreamTrack source-specific construction steps](#dfn-mediastreamtrack-source-specific-construction-steps) with track as parameter.

4.  Return track.

To initialize the underlying source of track to source, run the following steps:

1.  Initialize track.[`[[Source]]`](#dfn-source-0) to source.

2.  Initialize track's [\[\[Capabilities\]\]](#dfn-capabilities-0), [\[\[Constraints\]\]](#dfn-constraints), and [\[\[Settings\]\]](#dfn-settings-0), as specified in the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern).

To tie track source to `MediaDevices`, given source and mediaDevices, run the following steps:

1.  Add source to mediaDevices.[`[[mediaStreamTrackSources]]`](#dfn-mediastreamtracksources).

To stop all sources of a [global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#global-object), named globalObject, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  For each [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object track whose [relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#concept-relevant-global) is globalObject, set track's [`[[ReadyState]]`](#dfn-readystate) to "[`ended`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.ended)".

2.  If globalObject is a [`Window`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window), then for each source in globalObject's [associated `MediaDevices`](#dfn-associated-mediadevices).[`[[mediaStreamTrackSources]]`](#dfn-mediastreamtracksources), [stop](#source-stopped) source.

The [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* [stop all sources](#dfn-stop-all-sources) of a globalObject in the following conditions:

1.  If globalObject is a [`Window`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window) object and the [unloading document cleanup steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unloading-document-cleanup-steps) are executed for its [associated document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#concept-document-window).

2.  If globalObject is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#workerglobalscope) object and its [closing](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#dom-workerglobalscope-closing) flag is set to true.

An implementation may use a per-source reference count to keep track of source usage, but the specifics are out of scope for this specification.

To clone a track the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  Let track be the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object to be cloned.

2.  Let source be track's [`[[Source]]`](#dfn-source-0).

3.  Let trackClone be the result of [creating a MediaStreamTrack](#dfn-create-a-mediastreamtrack) with source and `null`.

4.  Set trackClone's [`[[ReadyState]]`](#dfn-readystate) to track's [`[[ReadyState]]`](#dfn-readystate) value.

5.  Set trackClone's [\[\[Capabilities\]\]](#dfn-capabilities-0) to a clone of track's [\[\[Capabilities\]\]](#dfn-capabilities-0).

6.  Set trackClone's [\[\[Constraints\]\]](#dfn-constraints) to a clone of track's [\[\[Constraints\]\]](#dfn-constraints).

7.  Set trackClone's [\[\[Settings\]\]](#dfn-settings-0) to a clone of track's [\[\[Settings\]\]](#dfn-settings-0).

8.  Run source [MediaStreamTrack source-specific clone steps](#dfn-mediastreamtrack-source-specific-clone-steps) with track and trackClone as parameters.

9.  Return trackClone.

There are two dimensions related to the media flow for a "[`live`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.live)" [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) : muted / not muted, and enabled / disabled.

Muted refers to the input to the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack). A [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) is [muted](#track-muted) when its source is muted, i.e. temporarily unable to provide the track with data. Live samples *MUST NOT* be made available to a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) while it is [muted](#track-muted).

The [muted](#track-muted) state is outside the control of web applications, but can be observed by the application by reading the [`muted`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-muted) attribute and listening to the associated events [`mute`](#event-mediastreamtrack-mute) and [`unmute`](#event-mediastreamtrack-unmute). The reasons for a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) to be muted are defined by its [source](#dfn-source).

For camera and microphone sources, the reasons to [mute](#dfn-muted-0) are [implementation-defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined). This allows user agents to implement privacy mitigations in situations like: the user pushing a physical mute button on the microphone, the user closing a laptop lid with an embedded camera, the user toggling a control in the operating system, the user clicking a mute button in the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) chrome, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) (on behalf of the user) mutes, etc.

On some operating systems, microphone access may get stolen from the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) when another application with higher-audio priority gets access to it, for instance in case of an incoming phone call on mobile OS. The [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *SHOULD* provide this information to the web application through [`muted`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-muted) and its associated events.

Whenever the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) initiates such an [implementation-defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) change for camera or microphone sources, it *MUST* queue a task, using the user interaction task source, to [set a track's muted state](#set-track-muted) to the state desired by the user.

Note

This does not apply to [sources](#dfn-source) defined in other specifications. Other specifications need to define their own steps to [set a track's muted state](#set-track-muted) if desired.

To set a track's muted state to newState, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* run the following steps:

1.  Let track be the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) in question.

2.  If track.[`[[Muted]]`](#dfn-muted) is already newState, then abort these steps.

3.  Set track.[`[[Muted]]`](#dfn-muted) to newState.

4.  If newState is `true` let eventName be [`mute`](#event-mediastreamtrack-mute), otherwise [`unmute`](#event-mediastreamtrack-unmute).

5.  [Fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) named eventName on track.

Enabled/disabled on the other hand is available to the application to control (and observe) via the [`enabled`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-enabled) attribute.

The result for the consumer is the same in the sense that whenever [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) is muted or disabled (or both) the consumer gets zero-information-content, which means silence for audio and black frames for video. In other words, media from the source only flows when a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object is both unmuted and enabled. For example, a video element sourced by a [`MediaStream`](#dom-mediastream) containing only muted or disabled [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack)s for audio and video, is playing but rendering black video frames in silence.

For a newly created [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object, the following applies: the track is always enabled unless stated otherwise (for example when cloned) and the muted state reflects the state of the source at the time the track is created.

A [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) has two states in its life-cycle: live and ended. A newly created [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) can be in either state depending on how it was created. For example, cloning an ended track results in a new ended track. The current state is reflected by the object's [`readyState`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-readystate) attribute.

In the live state, the track is active and media (or zero-information-content if the [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) is [muted](#track-muted) or [disabled](#track-enabled)) is available for use by consumers.

If the source is a device exposed by `navigator.mediaDevices.`[`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia)`()`, then when a track becomes either muted or disabled, and this brings all tracks connected to the device to be either muted, disabled, or stopped, then the UA *MAY*, using the device's [`deviceId`](#dom-mediadeviceinfo-deviceid), deviceId, set `navigator.mediaDevices.`[`[[devicesLiveMap]]`](#dfn-deviceslivemap)\[deviceId\] to `false`, provided the UA sets it back to `true` as soon as any unstopped track connected to this device becomes un-muted or enabled again.

When a "[`live`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.live)", [unmuted](#track-muted), and [enabled](#track-enabled) track sourced by a device exposed by [`getUserMedia`](#dom-mediadevices-getusermedia)`()` becomes either [muted](#track-muted) or [disabled](#track-enabled), and this brings *all* tracks connected to the device (across all [navigables](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#navigable) the user agent operates) to be either muted, disabled, or stopped, then the UA *SHOULD* relinquish the device within 3 seconds while allowing time for a reasonably-observant user to become aware of the transition. The UA *SHOULD* attempt to reacquire the device as soon as any live track sourced by the device becomes both [unmuted](#track-muted) and [enabled](#track-enabled) again, provided that track's [relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-global)'s [associated `Document`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#concept-document-window) [is in view](#dfn-is-in-view) at that time. If the document is not [in view](#dfn-is-in-view) at that time, the UA *SHOULD* instead queue a task to [mute](#track-muted) the track, and not queue a task to [unmute](#track-muted) it until the document comes [into view](#dfn-is-in-view). If reacquiring the device fails, the UA *MUST* [end the track](#ends-nostop) (The UA *MAY* end it earlier should it detect a device problem, like the device being physically removed).

Note

The intent is to give users the assurance of privacy that having physical camera (and microphone) hardware lights off brings, by aligning physical and logical “privacy indicators”, at least while the current document is the sole user of a device.

While other applications and documents using the device simultaneously may interfere with this intent at times, they do not interfere with the rules laid forth.

A [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object is said to *end* when the source of the track is disconnected or exhausted.

If all [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack)s that are using the same source are [ended](#track-ended), the source will be [stopped](#source-stopped).

After the application has invoked the [`stop`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-stop)`()` method on a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) object, or once the [source](#dfn-source) of a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) permanently ends production of live samples to its tracks, whichever is sooner, a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) is said to be ended.

For camera and microphone sources, the reasons for a source to [end](#track-ended) besides [`stop`](#dom-mediastreamtrack-stop)`()` are [implementation-defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) (e.g., because the user rescinds the permission for the page to use the local camera, or because the User Agent has instructed the track to end for any reason).

When a [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) track ends for any reason other than the `stop()` method being invoked, the [User Agent](#dfn-user-agent) *MUST* queue a task that runs the following steps:

1.  If track's [`[[ReadyState]]`](#dfn-readystate) has the value "[`ended`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.ended)" already, then abort these steps.

2.  Set track's [`[[ReadyState]]`](#dfn-readystate) to "[`ended`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.ended)".

3.  Notify track's [`[[Source]]`](#dfn-source-0) that track is [ended](#track-ended) so that the source may be [stopped](#source-stopped), unless other [`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) objects depend on it.

4.  [Fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) named [ended](#event-mediastreamtrack-ended) at the object.

If the end of the track was reached due to a user request, the event source for this event is the user interaction event source.

To invoke the device permission revocation algorithm with permissionName, run the following steps:

1.  Let tracks be the set of all currently "[`live`](#idl-def-MediaStreamTrackState.live)" `MediaStreamTrack`s whose permission associated with this kind of track ([`"camera"`](#dfn-camera) or [`"microphone"`](#dfn-microphone)) matches permissionName.

2.  For each track in tracks, [end](#ends-nostop) the track.

[`MediaStreamTrack`](#dom-mediastreamtrack) is a [constrainable object](#dfn-constrainable-object) as defined in the [Constrainable Pattern](#constrainable-interface) section. Constraints are set on tracks and may affect sources.

Whether ``[`Constraints`](#dom-constraints)`` were provided at track initialization time or need to be established later at runtime, the APIs defined in the [`ConstrainablePattern`](#dom-constrainablepattern) Interface allow the retrieval and manipulation of the constraints currently established on a track.

Once ended, a track will continue exposing a list of inherent constrainable track properties. This list contains `[deviceId](#def-constraint-deviceId)`, `[facingMode](#def-constraint-facingMode)` and `[groupId](#def-constraint-groupId)`.

```
[Exposed=Window]
